newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-POLL BACKS PELE IN DISPUTE OVER CITIZENSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLL BACKS PELE IN DISPUTE OVER CITIZENSHIP.

text.p: Brazilian soccer idol Pele failed to bring the 2004 Olympic Games to Rio de Janeiro on Friday but can take solace from the level of public support he enjoys in a dispute over his right to citizenship of Brasilia.

Left-wing members of Brasilia's state legislature this week blocked Pele's nomination for honorary citizenship of the country's capital. The award is conferred in recognition of special achievements and would not entitle Pele to any special treatment in the city.

The leftists said their decision was a protest against the former World Cup striker's refusal to accept 31-year-old shopworker Sandra Regina Machado as his love child, despite DNA tests backing her claim.
Lawmakers also said Pele, Brazil's sports minister, had done little to help improve the lot of blacks who make up the bulk of the country's poor.
But a poll published on Friday by newspaper Correio Braziliense showed 52 percent of 450 people interviewed favoured giving Pele the award with 38 percent against and 10 percent undecided.

Forty-seven percent agreed Pele's sporting achievements had helped reduce racism in Brazil but 61 percent said his refusal to recognise Machado as his daughter was bad for his image as a sportsman and public figure.
Pele, in Switzerland as part of Rio's unsuccessful bid to host the 2004 Olympics Games, was unavailable for comment.
